title: Evidence-lite statuspage update and tenant replay opt-in guidance
content:
Purpose and audience
This is a concise customer-facing status update and guided post-incident note intended for enterprise tenants affected by the regional inference degradation on 2028-03-14. It is written to: (1) give operators a compact timeline and minimal forensic evidence they can use to verify impact, (2) present safe options for replay / rollback / remediate at tenant level, and (3) list the next committed actions with owners and expected dates.

Executive summary (one paragraph)
On 2028-03-14 between 02:10 and 03:45 UTC, a subset of requests routed through our EU-west region experienced increased response latency and occasional truncated structured outputs for tenants using model route rwd/gptx-7b-v1. The issue affected ~3.2% of requests for impacted customers with an average p95 latency increase from 210ms to 4.2s during the window. No customer data was exfiltrated. We implemented a regional routing fallback and a hotfix patch to the runtime kernel selection logic; full mitigation was completed by 04:15 UTC. This note provides a short timeline, the current understanding of root cause, lightweight evidence you can verify, and tenant-level remediation choices.

Customer impact (scope and symptoms)
- Affected tenants: enterprise tenants on EU-west model route rwd/gptx-7b-v1 and those pinned to quantized-compat variants.
- Symptom profile: slow responses, non-deterministic token truncation in JSON/structured responses, and higher 429s for a small subset of burst traffic.
- Duration: 02:10–03:45 UTC; gradual recovery after operator routing change; full mitigation by 04:15 UTC.
- Business impact: throughput degradation for interactive features and delayed background batch jobs. Some customers observed partial failures inside streaming sessions.

Lightweight forensic evidence (what we can share now)
We adopt an "evidence-lite" approach for status pages to minimize operational friction for customers while giving them verifiable artifacts. Below are the verifiable artifacts we are attaching to the public status update and will make available to tenant contacts on request: 
1) Aggregated p50/p95/p99 latency charts for EU-west, timestamped and exported as CSV (range 01:30–05:00 UTC).
2) Sample request/response pairs (anonymized) that show token truncation behavior and the runtime error observed (kernel mismatch exception trace).
3) Kafka consumer offsets snapshot for router-phase metrics (offsets and partition IDs).
4) Short operator timeline (see timeline below) and the rollback/fallback actions that were executed.
These artifacts are sufficient to confirm whether a tenant observed the same symptom class. If tenants require deeper evidence (trace-level logs or per-request payloads), we provide an opt-in privacy-preserving replay package under an executed NDA and scoped data access agreement.

Root cause (current working hypothesis)
Our investigation points to a regression in the kernel selection heuristic introduced in runtime release v3.4.1. Under a specific sequence length distribution and a concurrent autoscaling event, the runtime chose a quantized kernel path that was incompatible with the model's KV cache layout for a short period. This produced two effects: (1) increased token generation latency due to repeated soft-fallback attempts, and (2) occasional structured output truncation when the KV cache pointer advanced incorrectly. The regression was triggered only when autoscale added instances while a continuous batching window was active, which is why only a subset of requests were impacted.

Immediate mitigations applied
- 02:25 UTC: We triggered policy-based routing to route new requests away from the specific EU-west pool causing errors.
- 02:40 UTC: Deployed a runtime hotfix that disabled the new kernel selection code path and forced a safe kernel choice for models in the affected class.
- 03:05 UTC: Increased backlog buffer to avoid mid-request cache pointer conflicts during autoscale events.
- 04:15 UTC: Verified steady-state metrics and progressively restored standard routing.

Tenant choices and recommended actions (concise)
We offer three safe remediation lanes for tenants. Each lane is designed to balance integrity, latency, and operational effort: 
1) Passive verification (no tenant action) — Recommended for most customers. We will notify you when full post-incident artifacts are available. Suitable if your workload experienced minimal customer-visible impact.
2) Evidence-lite self-verify (preferred for operators) — We will deliver the CSV latency charts and anonymized sample pairs to your security contact. Use these to confirm symptom match; if you observe matching anomalies, select lane 3.
3) Opt-in replay and reconstructed audit (requires tenant consent) — We will prepare a scoped replay package (anonymized, integrity tokens attached) that allows tenant teams to reconstruct individual request outcomes. This is recommended for customers who require deterministic verification for billing, compliance, or legal review.

API examples and tenant instructions (Evidence-lite self-verify)
- Download latency CSV from the status link (we will provide a signed URL).
- Use the provided sample request/response pairs to run a simple diff against your stored request outputs: 
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://signed.redwood.io/evidence/eu-west-latency-2028-03-14.csv" -o eu-west-latency.csv
- For truncated outputs, compare the JSON schema keys and the final token counts. If you see the same truncation pattern and timing alignment, open a dedicated support ticket with label INF-REGRESSION-EVIDENCE and attach the CSV segments.

Privacy, security, and governance notes
- No plaintext customer content will be published as part of the public statuspage. Sample pairs are sanitized and redacted by default.
- Opt-in replay requests require a short data access agreement and will only include request identifiers necessary for reconstruction; raw customer payloads will remain encrypted and scoped to the minimum necessary set.
- We will sign all shared artifacts with an operator integrity token to allow customers to verify authenticity.

Timeline (operator view)
- 01:58 UTC: autoscale event started (spike in new connections).
- 02:10 UTC: first elevated p95 observed; small number of truncated structured outputs reported by internal Canary.
- 02:25 UTC: routing change executed to divert new connections from impacted pool.
- 02:40 UTC: rollout of runtime hotfix v3.4.2 (kernel selection disabled).
- 03:05 UTC: backlog buffer adjustments completed.
- 03:45 UTC: p95s trending down; consumer claims begin to return to normal.
- 04:15 UTC: full recovery verified; routing reverted to standard policy.

Committed next steps and owners
- Forensic replay package template and release of evidence-lite bundle — Owner: Marco Alvarez — ETA: 2028-03-21
- Root cause final report and code revert PR merge verification — Owner: Priya Desai — ETA: 2028-03-23
- Enhance kernel-selection unit tests and autoscale integration tests — Owner: Elliot Wong (runtime) — ETA: 2028-04-05
- Tenant communications and optional NDA intake form — Owner: Claire Kim (customer-success) — ETA: 2028-03-20

FAQ (short)
Q: Will I be charged for requests affected by this incident?
A: We are assessing billing adjustments for customers who saw >10% request error/latency at peak. If you believe you qualify, please open a support ticket with label BILLING-INC-2028-03-14.

Q: Can you replay my requests without an NDA?
A: No. Replays require tenant consent and an access agreement. We provide evidence-lite artifacts without an NDA.

Q: How will I know if I was impacted?
A: If your tenant saw increased p95 latency during 02:10–03:45 UTC or observed truncated structured outputs, you were likely impacted. We will proactively email tenant primary contacts and include a signed evidence-lite bundle when available.

Contact and escalation
Primary contact: Claire Kim (customer-success) — claire.kim@redwood.ai
Escalations: Enterprise Success manager (Marco Alvarez) — marco.alvarez@redwood.ai
For legal/compliance intake: compliance@redwood.ai

Notes for internal use (short)
- Use this doc as the basis for the statuspage public blurb (keep the public message to the executive summary).
- Route evidence-lite artifacts to tenant security contacts only.
- Track all opt-in replay requests under Jira INF-REPLAY queue and ensure DAA is signed before data access.

END OF DRAFT
